name: markets
audience: people curious about money and markets who are not traders or insiders: stocks, oil, gold, currencies, bubbles, famous trades. Smart adults, so never childish or condescending.
tone: deadpan and funny, like telling a mate the stupidest true story you know about money; simple words, still factual; no hype, no price predictions, no financial advice
rules: Edu, 17 Nov 2026: "maybe NOT just all crypto... put like global markets stuff". This channel is the evening skit: stocks, oil, gold, currencies, inflation, bubbles and famous trading disasters, told as skits (script-guide 'Skits').

Never say or imply a price will go up or down, and never tell anyone to buy, sell or hold anything. Past prices with their dates are facts; the future is not. If the story invites a prediction, say plainly that nobody knows.

Every number on screen is in research.md with a source: an exchange or regulator record, a company filing, a central bank, or two major outlets (Reuters, Bloomberg, FT, WSJ, BBC). Old stories (before 1900) often come with legends: say 'the story goes' for anything historians doubt.
Explain any finance term the first time it's needed in one quick plain clause; max one new term per sentence; cut terms the story doesn't need.
Real people: tell what the record says, plainly. Nothing invented about them, nothing cruel. A regulator's finding or a court's verdict can be stated; a joke is never stated as a fact about them.
Keep current politicians and parties out of the hook and the caption (Instagram limits political content); a central bank or a government in a historical story is fine in the voice.
Mention Sonar at most once (the caption or the end tag), never as a hard sell.
Green only for up, red only for down; always pair colour with a text label.
style_source: edusancheez2005/sonar: IG_CONTENT_PLAYBOOK.md §2 (colours), §6 (Orca voice), §7 (data integrity), §8 (captions). Same account, same look.
caption_format: Line 1: the hook fact, keyword-rich (Instagram search reads captions).
1–2 lines with the real numbers and the date.
The suit guy and his friend are made up. The numbers are real.
Max 5 hashtags (Instagram's cap since Dec 2025): #StockMarket #Finance #Money #FinanceMemes #Sonar (swap one for a topic tag if it fits better).
Then a 'Sources:' block (posted as the first comment, not in the caption).

squeak.who: an off-screen voice, nobody on screen: a third party who has watched the whole thing and shouts the last word of the skit ("GET OUT!"), loud, a bit raised and held on the vowel, but clear enough that anyone can tell what is said. No character says it: no talk, no pointing, no mouth movement.
